helpCenter.subscription.headline: Let external lists keep your collections up to date
helpCenter.subscription.intro: A subscription records an external source to check over time and the collection that should receive its resources. It can track catalogs, sharing lists, or platform libraries, reducing repeated browsing and manual copying.
helpCenter.subscription.flow.title: Configure once, keep discovering
helpCenter.subscription.flow.source.desc: Choose a supported source type and fill in its required configuration.
helpCenter.subscription.flow.check.title: Check the external list
helpCenter.subscription.flow.check.desc: Enabled subscriptions are checked periodically; you can also check now.
helpCenter.subscription.flow.collect.des: Discovered resources enter the target collection; later additions can notify you.
helpCenter.subscription.flow.acquire.des: Automatic acquisition also needs collection settings, a lead, and a usable workflow.
helpCenter.subscription.card.title: Discovery, notifications, and acquisition are separate steps
helpCenter.subscription.card.check.title: Periodic background checks
helpCenter.subscription.card.check.desc: Keep the subscription enabled and the server running. The web page does not need to stay open.
helpCenter.subscription.card.notify.titl: Build a baseline, then watch for additions
helpCenter.subscription.card.notify.desc: The initial fill does not announce all existing items as new updates. Later additions can notify you and trigger relevant workflows.
helpCenter.subscription.card.acquire.des: Discovering a title or updating its information does not guarantee a download link or a local file.
helpCenter.subscription.boundary: If an item disappears from the source, its existing resource and local files are not automatically deleted. Subscriptions discover items, collections organize them and track progress, and acquisition workflows try to obtain files.
helpCenter.subscription.examples.title: Try one source first
helpCenter.subscription.examples.intro: First confirm that items reach the correct collection, then enable automatic acquisition if needed.
Scenario 1: Follow new works from a DLsite circle
You want to track a circle’s releases alongside the resources you already own.
Add a subscription from the collection’s Subscriptions tab, choose the DLsite circle source, and fill in the target as prompted.
Select the collection and check once
Explicitly select the target collection, save, and choose Check now. Leave automatic acquisition off while reviewing the initial list.
Keep the subscription enabled and the server running. Later releases enter the collection; check for an acquisition lead when you want the files.

Result: review the catalog and local collecting progress together. A catalog provides work information, not necessarily downloadable files; the initial import does not send a batch of “new work” notifications.
helpCenter.subscription.example.feed.tit: Scenario 2: Collect items from your Pixiv follow feed
helpCenter.subscription.example.feed.int: You want to keep discovering items from your follow feed without copying links each time.
helpCenter.subscription.example.feed.ste: Choose the Pixiv follow feed source, supply any required account or credentials as prompted, and select the collection.
Save and check now, then confirm the resources in the collection. If checking fails, review the error and fix the source configuration or login state.
After confirming that leads and a usable workflow are available, enable automatic acquisition in collection settings. Later additions can then enter the acquisition process.
helpCenter.subscription.example.feed.res: Result: discovery works independently of acquisition. Leave automatic acquisition off if you only want to organize the feed. Acquisition may still wait or fail to start when login, manual steps, or a suitable workflow are needed.
helpCenter.subscription.examples.target: Select the target collection explicitly, even when adding a subscription from inside a collection. Leaving it empty creates a new collection named after the subscription.
helpCenter.subscription.comparison.title: Subscriptions help with external lists that keep changing
helpCenter.subscription.comparison.intro: A URL is only the starting point. Subscriptions connect repeated checking with collection membership, while source access and downloading remain separate requirements.
helpCenter.subscription.comparison.bookm: Remembering to revisit and identifying what changed.
Enabled subscriptions check periodically and add discovered resources to a collection.
helpCenter.subscription.comparison.check: Copying changes again and comparing them with your library.
New entries become resource records that can be viewed with the collection’s owned and missing states.
helpCenter.subscription.comparison.downl: Creating tasks only after finding links
New titles without links may never enter your collecting list.
Discover and keep the resource first, then acquire it manually or automatically when the requirements are met.
helpCenter.subscription.comparison.tip: Subscriptions require a supported source type and valid configuration. Check the result when one fails; repeated checks cannot supply missing credentials, access, or acquisition workflows.
helpCenter.subscription.concept.source.s: The source determines where to check; the target collection determines where resources go.
helpCenter.subscription.concept.source.l:
A subscription includes a source type, the configuration it requires, its enabled state, and a target collection. Inputs, account requirements, and returned content vary by source; arbitrary URLs are not all supported.
Catalog sources focus on work entries, sharing lists may provide acquisition leads, and platform libraries describe platform entries. None automatically means local files exist.
Select the target collection when creating a subscription. Leaving it empty creates a collection named after the subscription, so check this field even when starting from another collection.
helpCenter.subscription.concept.source.e: Example: choose “Circle A works” as the target of a DLsite circle subscription. Discovered entries go there; an existing download folder does not select a collection for you.
Periodic checks and the initial fill
Record existing entries first, then identify later additions.

Enabled subscriptions are checked periodically while the server is running; the browser page need not stay open. Use Check now to verify configuration and inspect the current result.
The initial fill establishes a baseline without announcing all existing entries as new updates. Later additions can send notifications and trigger relevant workflows.
Entries disappearing from the external list do not automatically delete existing resources or local files. A failed check does not mean those resources have been lost.

Example: the first check finds 20 entries and adds them without announcing all 20 as newly published. A later check finds entry 21 and handles it as a subsequent addition. Attempts to obtain files still depend on acquisition settings.
helpCenter.subscription.concept.acquisit: Subscriptions discover resources; acquisition workflows try to obtain their files.

Automatic acquisition requires the collection setting to be enabled, a lead for the newly added missing resource, and a usable acquisition workflow. Updating a title or catalog information alone does not download files.
Some sources provide only catalogs without usable download leads. Even a started task may need an account, password, manual action, or inbox handoff; not every link can complete automatically.
The initial fill skips new-update notifications, but its added resources may still trigger acquisition when enabled. Leave automatic acquisition off if you only want to review the list first.

Example: a catalog subscription discovers a title with no acquisition lead. It remains missing in the collection. When a usable lead and workflow become available, you can try acquiring it; the title alone cannot download a file.
